answer: Picture trust as a terrace garden: each new agent starts on the lowest step and only climbs when it crosses a bridge — a one-time attestation anchored to a scarce external resource that no identity can reuse. Real earning power unlocks only on the upper steps, reached after a slow voyage of peer-audited work across many epochs. A sybil farm must fund a separate bridge crossing per fake and age each one up the whole voyage, so cost grows linearly per head while an honest agent pays the toll just once.
